record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let Topk be the category of T0 spaces with continuous maps preserving all existing irreducible suprema. Let KBSob be the category of k-bounded sober spaces, where a space is k-bounded sober if every nonempty irreducible closed set whose supremum exists is the closure of a unique point. Is KBSob reflective in Topk?

evidence.quote: Question 7.21. ([37]) Is KBSob reflective in Topk ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbf{Top}_k$ denote the category whose objects are $T_0$ topological spaces and whose morphisms are continuous maps $f\colon X\to Y$ that preserve all existing irreducible suprema, i.e., whenever $A\subseteq X$ is an irreducible closed subset whose supremum (in the specialization order of $X$) exists and equals $x$, the supremum of $\overline{f(A)}$ exists in $Y$ and equals $f(x)$. Call a $T_0$ space $X$ k-bounded sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset $A\subseteq X$ whose supremum (in the specialization order) exists in $X$ is the closure $\overline{\{x\}}$ of a unique point $x\in X$. Let $\mathbf{KBSob}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_k$ whose objects are the k-bounded sober spaces.

Determine whether $\mathbf{KBSob}$ is a reflective subcategory of $\mathbf{Top}_k$; equivalently, whether for every object $X$ of $\mathbf{Top}_k$ there exists a k-bounded sober space $\widehat{X}$ and a morphism $\eta_X\colon X\to\widehat{X}$ in $\mathbf{Top}_k$ such that every morphism from $X$ to a k-bounded sober space factors uniquely through $\eta_X$.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work shows that $\mathbf{KBSob}$ is not reflective in the category $\mathbf{Top}_0$ of all $T_0$ spaces with all continuous maps (a $T_0$ space lacking any k-bounded sobrification has been constructed), and that $\mathbf{KBSob}$ is reflective in the smaller category $\mathbf{QKBSob}$ of qk-bounded sober spaces. However, the specific question of reflectivity in $\mathbf{Top}_k$ (with morphisms preserving existing irreducible suprema) is not explicitly resolved in the sources located, so the status remains unclear.

status_evidence.title: Nonexistence of k-bounded sobrification
status_evidence.snippet: the category KBSob of all k-bounded sober spaces is not a reflective subcategory of the category Top0 of all T0 spaces; KBSob is a full reflective subcategory of QKBSob
status_evidence.claim: KBSob fails to be reflective in Top0 but is reflective in QKBSob; the question for Topk is not explicitly resolved there.

status_evidence.title: Bounded Sobriety and k-Bounded Sobriety
status_evidence.snippet: Study of k-bounded sober spaces and their categorical properties.
status_evidence.claim: Background reference defining k-bounded sober spaces and discussing categorical setting.
